notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #8: City and Fortress Building
notes.content:
[p]Some of you have asked how city and fortress building works in [b]Stormbinders[/b].[/p][p]The answer: classic castle building – starting from a small [b]village[/b] and growing into the [b]capital of your kingdom[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/e0ace9db6fb9be9f60703090466c0dc47356aa9c.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/ad3292629be96748a9f2ec601174401c03096074.jpg"][/img]Each castle has:[/p][list][*][p]A [b]shared set of buildings[/b] that work the same across all factions.[/p][/*][*][p]A [b]unique set[/b] tied to each faction.[/p][/*][/list][p]For example: one faction can skip upgrade requirements, while another might convert weaker units into skeletons.[/p][p]In total, with upgrades included, each faction reaches [b]around 50 building options[/b] – that’s nearly two months of development in gameplay time! Different strategies will definitely encourage skipping or delaying certain upgrades. 😉[/p][h2]Castle Levels[/h2][p]To prevent “optimal rush” tactics (army → resources → top-tier units in week 2), we added [b]city levels[/b].
You need a set number of buildings upgraded before moving to the next tier.[/p][p]It slows things down just enough so strategies stay flexible, but high-level units aren’t instantly accessible.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/fdb972a4c794c25b44cd3e3f64e38253ce11a218.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/39d9c05f6d847520af4b8a6bac819f84c332a623.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Why 2D Castles?[/h2][p]From the production side, we considered several approaches:[/p][list][*][p]Skip castles entirely, just UI. (Didn’t fit the spirit of the game)[/p][/*][*][p]Minimal 2D/3D placeholders. (Uninspiring like a game with VI number in tittle) [/p][/*][*][p]Full 3D with cinematic assets. (Way out of scope)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Stylized 2D art.[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]We chose 2D art – the only realistic option.

What we didn’t expect? The [b]time cost[/b].[/p][p]Creating 4 castles took our artist over a year:[/p][list][*][p]Dozens of buildings per castle.[/p][/*][*][p]Upgrades, placement, adjustments.[/p][/*][*][p]Handling different storms and seasons.[/p][/*][/list][p]It was a huge challenge, but worth it.[/p][h2]Castles on the Adventure Map[/h2][p]We also added a [b]visual indicator[/b] of a castle’s level directly on the world map.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/e74388f6decf87e521e5b34be6201960fef4af55.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/a2425568cbfd11015a8e089b8fce750569b80bcd.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/c47e867f0dab5fb34cd68e23658e0b6555738d7d.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/6dcdf9664dd669f390d0aefc1af8e18861ee3083.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/c05bbbaf32137ebd81d100897da28c6d01c1e2c3.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]It doesn’t add much mechanically (you can always check the UI), but… it just looks cool. Sometimes you do things [i]only[/i] because they look cool.[/p][h2]Sieges and War Machines[/h2][p]Of course, beautiful castles are only half the story.[/p][p]Stormbinders also features [b]sieges[/b], where mighty war machines come into play:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/052a341cf7d9ad31d8e98dacdf9ea0bfeda2ac90.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/d1707f4b723b738dc49283b06747822a8c217b3b.png"][/img][/p][p]…and suddenly, your lovely gates and towers don’t look so safe anymore.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/f4caa82faac6290aaef906e141417752f911304a.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/8f5d10fc47707c69976355a5d6840237bdcfbd60.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/cedf481e0a501bc2c51e968a3b23d845b6423f63.png"][/img][/p][p]
That’s the big picture of how cities and fortresses evolve in [b]Stormbinders[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]And for a little fun:
Try to spot the placeholder Grail in the screenshot below.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/3364fe5d81a52fbd57aae3557c210797b76cf0b2.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Wishlist Stormbinders[/b]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink] [/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #7: Combining Magic Schools with Dynamic Storm Effects
notes.content:
[p]In Stormbinders, we wanted to push tactical combat one step further. That's why we introduced a third player into every battle: Storms.[/p][p][b]Yes, you read that right.[/b][/p][p]We designed a dynamic Stormbinding system that changes the flow of every match. It doesn’t just affect the battlefield – it transforms the rules of engagement across the entire world map.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/e2088acf8b0b974e6539cce99bb27b76a05f2859.png"][/img][/p][h3]So… what do storms actually do in a 1v1 fight?[/h3][p]Depending on the currently active Global Storm, you’ll notice several things happening as soon as a battle starts:[/p][list][*][p]Random storm zones (whirlwinds, fire swirls, ice fields) are generated on the battlefield[/p][/*][*][p]The active storm casts random spells inherited from its elemental theme
(e.g. Blizzards during a Spirit Storm, Meteors during a Firestorm – you get the idea)[/p][/*][*][p]Certain units and spells get buffed or nerfed, depending on the storm[/p][/*][*][p]Your battlefield positioning and strategy may need to change on the fly[/p][/*][/list][p]In other words, Stormbinding rewrites the rules of combat.[/p][p]But it doesn't end there.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/e1d975bb6e157fc49c60ef85a0b991e44a4f5485.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Storms affect the world map too[/h3][p]Storms aren't just flavor – they actively impact exploration, pacing, and decision-making on the world map:[/p][list][*][p]Certain areas may become inaccessible or dangerous during a storm[/p][/*][*][p]Storms might disrupt your supply chains or restrict mobility[/p][/*][*][p]Some units thrive in specific storm conditions (e.g. Imps during Firestorms)[/p][/*][*][p]Others become vulnerable (e.g. Empyrium units during Lightning Storms)[/p][/*][/list][p]So now, every move you make is context-sensitive.
Should you risk entering that fight while the enemy has elemental advantage?
Or should you wait, change the storm, and turn the tides?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/8ad301be108400fdf1634a3ebeebd6d9aa00b97d.png"][/img][/p][p][b]And yes – you can cast your own storms[/b][/p][p]As you progress through the Stormbinding skill tree, you’ll unlock the ability to manipulate the storm system yourself:[/p][list][*][p]At first, players are introduced to a "Local Storm" spell – a small-scale effect that helps them understand storm mechanics visually[/p][/*][*][p]From Turn 6 onward, players can level up their Stormbinding abilities[/p][/*][*][p]On Turn 14, a random Global Storm strikes the map – unless the player triggers one themselves before that[/p][/*][*][p]Players can switch between storm types based on their talents and spell synergy[/p][/*][*][p]Each storm creates a temporary environmental shift, turning the map and battles into new challenges[/p][/*][/list][p][b]This creates deep individual playstyles based on:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Unit synergy with elemental storms[/p][/*][*][p]Class talents that scale differently with storm effects[/p][/*][*][p]Tactical foresight – keeping storm mana for map control or using it all for powerful burst spells[/p][/*][*][p]RNG – yes, each game is unique thanks to random neutral units, buildings, storm patterns, and events[/p][/*][/list][p][b]With every decision – to wait, to cast, to rush in – the storm becomes a living system you interact with.

[/b]But don’t worry – you can keep it simple
We also know not everyone wants to calculate:[/p][p]“Fireball deals X% base damage + Y% bonus during Firestorm – Z% because you’re fighting on frozen terrain.”[/p][p]For many players, it’s simply:[/p][p]“My Fireball hits harder right now – great!”
Or: “It did less, but it still killed things – I’m happy.”[/p][p]And that’s totally fine.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/d8a6aeacb60191763292b95f54a863f8a511721d.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Player agency – opt in or opt out[/h3][p]Let’s face it: not every player wants to think about storms every time they fight. We get that.[/p][p]That’s why we added dozens of gameplay options that let you opt in or opt out of storm mechanics.
Want a more classic turn-based strategy feel? Turn them off.
Want chaos and adaptation? Turn them all on.[/p][p]The worst thing a game can do is force you to play a certain way. That’s not our design philosophy.

[b]Wishlist Stormbinders Now[/b]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #6: Underground Exploration
notes.content:
[h2]One Map, Infinite Layers[/h2][p]In Stormbinders, you don’t switch between separate maps. The entire world, including both surface and underground areas, exists on one continuous map. That means everything works seamlessly: units, storms, seasonal changes, and terrain effects apply across every layer.[/p][p]This is made possible by our multilayering system, which lets us nest any number of levels within each other. You can have undergrounds below undergrounds, hidden chambers within ruins, or underwater tunnels beneath lava caverns. Each layer runs within the same map and can have its own biome, rules, or events.[/p][p]In practice? We can create any type of dungeon labyrinth, vertically.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfT40L3wh7g23BtULAEyAiNnn-YZLCKGRvAN4Dmyns3AQ9XE118eqaMOc-uDUA5YU94wy0Kt4JfxWWEzZgmjC9daerdF8ns-6bM9tbZ6hhxAT4MfgZKICu822H_jH4i_fXcJQMp0XYm_byyzsowteY?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfsQelKGWW9Eoysb-gq7xp-Vs_twZraPmPJCDIBIjy6DQaMnN-mM-rTHDrXu3PNuo_EdXoUl5nq7NZysN3RvBvWY3hqWC8OOFDRinbbWDfssxMI74Ph26fMQrambOR4FkqktSjMiKEghlQROYsLkJ0?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][h2]Any biome, even below ground[/h2][p]Every layer can have a completely different biome. Want a frozen cave beneath a scorching desert? Or a ruined city below an enchanted forest? No problem. Each layer supports unique weather, movement rules, terrain appearance, and atmosphere.[/p][p]This means exploration is never predictable. Under every mountain, a different world might be waiting.[/p][h2]Tactical and narrative potential[/h2][p]The multilayering system isn’t just visual, it’s a gameplay and storytelling tool:[/p][list][*][p]Hidden factions or entire underground bases[/p][/*][*][p]Ancient ruins that require finding an entrance below the surface[/p][/*][*][p]Changing combat rules (e.g. storms don’t reach underground, but other effects do)[/p][/*][*][p]Seasonal and weather rules that behave differently depending on the layer[/p][/*][/list][p]Undergrounds in Stormbinders are a fully integrated part of the gameplay with their own depth and mechanics.[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdlP9s8LGi_XX-8MV8cfus4_F3Q_mKnXSExrUksSKAK3lIx9dPRsP0Z0YtoefYVk0dz1aqy7PmNrQnDqTafQ8Fbp6d4jYXy9-59fCf_YEP5jIozJSRjqJ-i5AVx16H-19k9PP_rAEoM6gu-kP_qQQ?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfPA-HI1O_lkAS158NavgTg9Jz90TqMZ2C4MWdmTkTcO40slURsZOXjmw2vL8R7eZe1UtOJSsBbxMW-ExN7SDa13t11GurIJIlo8kQZ80_b6gbWdNdXOmXoX50J-wjGRYS1yl0rZxGF2bP8wVFGNLc?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeZZDwBqWSKUoeQ0KZ9J_MDPBxTQ7bcdjfQkagaqqPfzhlwjRTZSTvEHYSTP6jHz29cxXPOg3p69krPfZJgTsl6EGd3G9jWLbYlGTwRAdrMPxtAHhyfVGsM1hb4s0LVKlr9b9euVSCHlDhU1IqpC64?key=h2fyhWdQPbmJYlqxMpbMHQ"][/img][/p][h2]Stormbinding and layered weather[/h2][p]Yes, Stormbinding works across layers, but not all storms pass through all levels. 

This means certain magical conditions, buffs, and storm-dependent units may act very differently underground.[/p][p]It adds a whole new layer of planning: sometimes it’s better to retreat below ground when a Deadly Storm approaches.[/p][h2]Tools for campaign creators and modders[/h2][p]Thanks to this system:[/p][list][*][p]Designers can build complex, multi-level locations full of secret paths, teleporters, and mysteries[/p][/*][*][p]Campaigns can guide players through different layers – like “chapters” of the same world[/p][/*][*][p]Modders will be able to use multilayering to create unique and immersive worlds full of hidden stories[/p][/*][/list][p]If you’re wondering why we went through the trouble of making it this flexible… it’s simple: we wanted deserts and forests in the underground too. [/p][h2]Custom underground rules[/h2][p]Inspired by the classics, and going against today’s trend of oversimplification, our undergrounds are not just cosmetic layers.[/p][p]Each underground level can have its own set of gameplay rules that change how other systems behave:[/p][list][*][p]Different movement rules (e.g. tighter corridors, no flying allowed)[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced visibility and spell range[/p][/*][*][p]No weather effects – or alternate effects like soul echoes or earthquakes[/p][/*][*][p]Limited access to certain units or spells[/p][/*][*][p]Modified economy – different resources, nerfed buildings, or limited construction[/p][/*][/list][p]This makes underground exploration a strategic experience of its own. It’s not just a change of scenery – it’s a different way to play the game entirely.

[b]Wishlist Now[/b][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #5: Hero Design
notes.content:
[h2]Hero Classes – Archetypes with a Twist
[/h2][p]When we started designing our class system, we asked ourselves a simple question:
[i]What if each class could evolve and change over time?[/i][/p][p]That’s how our branching class paths were born.[/p][p]For example, here’s the progression path for a [b]Warrior archetype[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Knight (Might)[/b] → evolves into → [b]Paladin (Might & Magic)[/b] [i]or[/i] [b]Duelist (Might & Might)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Paladin[/b] can become → [b]Inquisitor (Might & Magic & Magic)[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Duelist[/b] can become → [b]Warlord (Might & Might & Might)[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]So a single warrior archetype in a given faction has 5 stages of progression.
Add the Mage archetype to that, and you end up with 10 unique class paths per faction.[/p][p]At any stage, you can [i]lock in[/i] your current class – preserving your chosen specialization and its unique stat growth, skill trees, and talent distribution.[/p][p]It might seem like a small detail – but when you multiply 2 archetypes per faction × 4 factions, you end up with [b]40 distinct hero classes[/b].
Each of them comes with:[/p][list][*][p]unique active and passive talents[/p][/*][*][p]different ways of rolling for key skills[/p][/*][*][p]separate stat growth curves[/p][/*][*][p]and a ton of micro differences that make each class feel distinct.[/p][/*][/list][p]Each level-up doesn’t just raise stats, it unlocks [b]new class paths[/b] and options that are exclusive to your chosen combination.

But don’t worry – if you prefer a straightforward experience, you can mostly ignore this complexity.
Yes, it [i]does[/i] have an impact – and yes, min-maxers will have a field day with their spreadsheets.
But if you just want to play and level up your hero, you’ll still feel stronger and more capable, without needing to dive into all the systems.[/p][p]Power players will find deep optimization.
Everyone else? A hero who just gets better with time.[/p][p]
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd6lINYRv-ifMs1_goJnukqupaPiMHQ99hH5VlMQmygviy6eb4LoWMm6eGJ_3fsri9aSR24YKJQfwmH-8Z9KgZDXQgdq1WGyPjy8xMQ0ZSvKf0xg1LT2Q0vdiatCH_qsJKaD4DTP3D4g-Cm9AvuMQ?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeSLFA2kOvv0xSHxvbeUdc83WQsBhRRQV2IbPhaexf_EnPKWwwXHx_HQGNjyTzhrFGyVaRnIwo6RSWUW_wD3hrvaq_NVmsHsLzSJ1t2uPbWXzVQ8d1oh8eud_DneXk2HEaybJjXS2KJ6Tr307kUW5c?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXctA9wv-G-5onF66V5aZRoXcrPNm5Bh_o-S4MurM_oHMX1E_G3H989601I0L6VGH0k6sqFyEm3UcglKoE7ktoQdHr0h4vQhM0Hh-RazI_OxvVe3ZyhoIuIpcEdgNGIeP9UKag2dASks-WyFZcIkp0w?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeoG9NaKo8TWSzQ2MJHFPeUfnHbTfk_djWyinnZ_iwQXQlMrYfWMrjeLv05iV5cxZ7XDYpr45AwavvDFuVP4WNOuuEx4bLiKV3pP4SPaRE2M9hnoXZyaJ_3mel0tp2yLBfx-x6hkX66435_49GAnw?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdmd0YpLUvHGsebxoizkED-z39ofD2IouY4vzMETenKZTgHowdN1dpsSp2BseKsfU969WiUHf_rqAOZX2cL9VtcFCXlG1cRuS5NLHfQfFa7jtaK2sqQa-GGc14Hg4o8hYJPg7DhIyvDF5OvI9H5Eqo?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe52pDCKqmE7uHH09CtU33V5x42CHDPir2Q9r5qsmtZTo7Rq9LDhGA1muz9mQeePr259giUZdJ_GDcnrHdanMKmnAWx5YhZ4BQY5KHg3Ps_VMZil8IJW3gNK6PARDc-F2m7_hOdggTkEI4t2XZAjBw?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][/p][h2]
Talent Trees – Three Layers of Personalization
[/h2][p]Classes are just the beginning. The real fun in hero development comes from talents.
And we won’t pretend we invented something new here. There are dozens of talent models out there, but the one that truly stuck with us was from Heroes of Might and Magic V.[/p][p]Yes, we’re talking about a [b]Mastery Talent System[/b], where every main skill unlocks secondary perks, and it’s up to the player to decide how to build the perfect setup.[/p][p]Each hero in [i]Stormbinders[/i] grows using three interconnected types of talents:[/p][list][*][p][b]Faction Talents[/b] – shared by all heroes from the same faction, supporting their unique philosophy (e.g. better necromancy for Immortus, stronger storm manipulation for Astrion)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Class Talents[/b] – core talents based on the hero’s role (mage, warrior, leader), which define their main combat approach[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hero Talents[/b] – unique to the individual hero; these often break the rules and open powerful combos
[i](think: teleport for 0 mana, fire spells boosted during storms, or free summoning perks)[/i][/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks to this structure, we ended up with [b]hundreds of possible builds[/b].[/p][p]This means:[/p][list][*][p]One [b]warrior[/b] from Immortus can play completely differently than a warrior from Empyrium[/p][/*][*][p]One [b]mage[/b] from Helion might focus on summoning demons, while another goes full fire explosion spam[/p][/*][*][p]And the mix of [b]faction + class + unique hero talents[/b] creates dozens of playstyles and synergies[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcOFKc-W8zlnSXoR2EF_bpN1lHY2L3TDeQGtmW9lhs33UjgyAlx895RGmlPxvWQo65QSjdk0XOurQ8dqUIc6DI6VFg3bYd50xyTY94zLDmebrYcGZxN1cSFjeBckIrELT449G1_VfNRP7dT47fVGA?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfYV-slTdXX1YvKLxCITSbEmp69JNWajAqfqhh-XV7QqM2XeMak6-oMkVA5iIV7rFkRjML42OSktzFPXjMFIS97XozmjCTP1sY9aPfSjTl9UNRZ7G_T6Twc03bnp6Tg4XshCPphuXkQXXOBNVwG40k?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd7zj8hSrze4fOtErz5cvthA9XBD0Sq1oBKDBfJt4IRJNKmcPUjG21iaC9l6MGmg3YdLDvNwpcphapOgHXeGHZRo2p-wcMrRAGOdkx1cWlsN99qm2n602u_WmPYTNs6HLl9mbn1cPDTi5hT_eTR61E?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcHfLDlcW3iZIcSBy_T2-IFmeM9qGvnhW0N9i4nqBeTrKZE3gEMXIgvCoJw5y69C4Q9MRyqHzyFk14ibzWs1mf4pa3PyNg9P6eqV2my_dmDFO3mQePT0MQHRI_3gHr8qcFXVpMKfUlPId5y27Kwxg?key=SXbQuDW7GcG4aTwr8phd5Q"][/img][/p][h2]
RPG in Numbers – Details That Matter
[/h2][p]Talents are fun, but what do they actually [i]do[/i]?[/p][p]For some players, they’re just numbers, but for us they’re pure gameplay.[/p][p]Each class in [i]Stormbinders[/i] grows differently. Every time they level up, they gain [b]unique attribute points[/b]:[/p][list][*][p][b]Mages[/b] gain more spell power and faster mana regeneration[/p][/*][*][p][b]Warriors[/b] get better leadership, durability, and initiative[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hybrids[/b] unlock special combinations and talents that mix both styles[/p][/*][/list][p]Sounds nerdy? [b]Good.[/b]
[i]Stormbinders[/i] is a game built to be mastered, for those who want to dig deep into stats and theorycrafting. But don’t worry, it’s completely optional.[/p][p]You can also play on instinct and still have a great time.
The numbers are there when you want them, but they never get in your way.[/p][h2]
Heroes and How They Look – Quantity over Decoration
[/h2][p]While developing [i]Stormbinders[/i], we asked ourselves:
[i]How should we approach the design of heroes?[/i][/p][p]Should we create a small number of super-polished characters, with high production values and unique visuals like the biggest AAA studios do? [/p][p]Or should we follow the spirit of classic games, where there are [b]many heroes[/b], maybe not all visually unique, but differentiated by starting talents and class archetypes?[/p][p]We chose the second path and we believe it fits [i]Stormbinders[/i] best.[/p][p]By focusing on [b]quantity and variety[/b], we can easily add new heroes in future updates, each with new combinations of talents, classes, and specializations. This gives us more flexibility and replayability.[/p][p]So yes, [b]some heroes share their visuals[/b].
But what really matters is [b]how they play[/b].[/p][p]Every hero has:[/p][list][*][p]Their own set of talent options[/p][/*][*][p]Their own growth path[/p][/*][*][p]Their own unique combination of faction and class powers[/p][/*][/list][p]And if we ever want to add 10, 20, or even 50 more heroes, we can.[/p][h2]
Our Vision for Stormbinders
[/h2][p]At this point, we hope you’re starting to see what this game is all about.

We want to bring back that [b]magical feeling[/b] we had growing up – and take it even further. With systems you’ve never seen before. With dynamic weather, RPG-like hero growth, and deep tactical options.[/p][p][i]Stormbinders[/i] is our love letter to the past, and a bold step into something new.

We hope you’ll enjoy discovering it as much as we’re enjoying creating it.
[/p][p][b]WISHLIST NOW[/b]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #4: Unique Faction Abilities
notes.content:
[p]After introducing the core identities and philosophies of Stormbinders’ four factions in the last entry, we’re now ready to focus on [b][i]how[/i] each faction plays[/b] thanks to their exclusive powers and faction mechanics. [/p][p]These distinctive abilities shape your strategies in meaningful ways and will lead directly into our upcoming topic: how we create distinct heroes, classes, and ability trees.
[/p][h2]Empyrium - Kingdom of the Sun and Order[i]
[/i][b]
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcgKhnXqKdQCl8AVxbxbMQD7mN4S_6emG_FinWL3o3DI69_BzliOz6NT9j3Gg4PoP3ItR2ThMuL113I_FXPWo8b5JUbavjYqYDIgQIkX1IPbXkkZGQxFxz1o-6Pk0cFWz7ZBPKeWWkWnnLo5EA6oHc?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img][/b][/h2][p]We’ve already mentioned that Empyrium believes in structure, balance, and order. These humans hold onto tradition while using advanced technology to keep chaos at bay. Their empire may be divided, but their armies still march forward – proud and powerful.
[/p][p]In gameplay, Empyrium is the most balanced faction in the game. Their armies are elite and expensive, but each unit has a clear purpose. They can adapt to offense or śdefense depending on the situation. Ideal for players who want full tactical control with flexible options – from strong cavalry to siege machines.[/p][h3][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf1CEffasLkRyg-xc4Vyx67tQ4XtKqlAPGnRDy0mYK5b-Iqr04HAIo1525EN8o2hSXdS7YZl-ySYACobO1KLNNrPKmT8_47RaIiZGHc2ofzw1azHuPSEEO2OAYhOCdQD5-mJvp6V-U1roIYqoo3eLg?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img]

[/h3][h3]Faction Ability: Light of Renewal[/h3][p]Empyrium can bring fallen living units back to life. By using divine light and technology, they can restore their most important troops right when it matters most – turning the tide of a battle or holding the line during a siege.
[/p][h2]Astrion - Guardians of the Magic Weave

[/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcmlX26VBwVffrUO72fyMyXszRS097pzKtWWyYwXsk0SMRqYLjpEtYuKcoJblTrSZ_Plx6v3_yYb5rlEVC3triJJnTBB6ET8FLWGbPzjr1dLRl9mjPJgzGNgHZh26Jir5JMdP4kxLnJ6xKGXFnS4r0?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img][/p][p]In our previous entry, we introduced Astrion as protectors of the Magic Weave – the very fabric of reality. [/p][p]When the world began to tear apart, they dedicated themselves to restoring balance. They fight with discipline, wisdom, and harmony, believing that magic must be used responsibly.[/p][p]Astrion armies are small but elite. Every unit is valuable. This faction rewards players who plan ahead, protect their troops, and use defensive or control-based magic. Astrion shines in situations where timing, preparation, and positioning matter most.[/p][h3][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeLx2nb2mg6JIA5iD_H7QRxy8TLaIMogmjbeLkCaJUPq4yZVxknQNzD-KUVw_cLH557sUGQTi11X9xXksxi2woXwOd7EIrx2c44MEH07C6g0GKa27YbUmGd0EJZL5rsQ0gY_LtgrCKwnxSDzk8S2R4?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img]

[/h3][h3]Faction Ability: Storm Echo[/h3][p]Astrion can channel energy from magical storms. When stormbinding events happen on the map, their spells become stronger – gaining extra shields, reduced costs, or bonus effects. They can also predict storm cycles better than others, giving them a planning advantage.
[/p][h2]Helion - the World Burners[b]
[/b][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdmmHnxTaGXmC3Mq-H6oY94VTHeeQXfxDLnWveWO5H0u01VA3NB4qHSU3B80GFO0RS1vMzCquI0vGxv2-nNaJxa9aDOH9ZherZqCChTCwWnQJuFQ30nhZ04HpsZ18KtQYKjkwhVMwaEmPRCuIeInA?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img][/h2][p]Where others see a world in crisis, Helion sees opportunity. They aim not to fix the world, but to burn it down and rebuild it in fire. Their lands were consumed by chaos, and under their dark leader Malgrim, they now spread destruction across Azium. Strength is all that matters. Fire, blood, and domination.[/p][p][b]
[/b]Helion is made for aggressive players. They rely on fast attacks, brutal fire magic, and demon summoning. They thrive on pressure – pushing enemies with overwhelming force and turning every battle into a wildfire. Quick decisions and constant offense are their trademarks.[/p][h3][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeBNg1FyJEUdPsDgAb_mwLEsmNcJHtMiA5BpGOAoPZRMApq8TdOH5_Yo-q7tCm_2tHWSMhVP17I2py5zBgiVQ-Kai9GHVqYOY_aA-6TEhNydNBJNRiU8i1VpjXZhXyf5w4WBgGGoNnxjZwleUGdKhc?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img]

[/h3][h3]Faction Ability: Infernal Consumption[/h3][p]Helion absorbs the souls of defeated enemies. These souls become magic fuel, which can be used to cast stronger spells or summon more demons. The more blood is spilled – the stronger Helion becomes. Even a lost battle can be turned into a magical advantage.
[/p][h2]Immortus - Lords of the Death and Rebirth[/h2][p][b]
[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc7kdB-zjCl8KDVZedMrnJCcT7i_HoC2033VKFnogLV_gYG1pC4jbsmqXDA8iMq_vaZgjgvLKYvxrkY18WGpsiMKjEl8dRzYenhcIAKRyvJpXZjtCamV1gIu-GPeJP5zhTlsXh6SfR-xIo0TYqsJw?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img]
[/b]For Immortus, death isn’t the end, it’s just the next stage. Their world was shattered, but they endured. Calm, cold, and eternal. Their goal is to rebuild the world under their rule – by mastering both life and death.[/p][p][b]
[/b]Immortus wins through numbers. Their undead armies are cheap and keep coming back. Every battle strengthens them – because every death becomes another soldier. Ideal for players who like slow, inevitable control and overwhelming their enemies through attrition.[/p][p][b][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcTY7x-bA2S-Hcc24w1By0tEIc_MNsFW9Q4cDaBXwkeJ_QQGqjGdMt0MlnYNT2tqoCP3oOhXjuGp6FBrKjckzWkz25aZ0AgE6Vy-piBkQ8Jh-y8vvwFKM3XVt7YQ2tCdIUIrXbdZHX_TZW1TtCLh70?key=Se6hfcZm_POd99X7ExV7wQ"][/img]

[/b][/p][h3]Faction Ability: Eternal Call[/h3][p]Immortus can raise any dead unit – friend or foe – as a skeleton. Over time, their undead horde becomes unstoppable. With the help of the "Pit of Bones" structure, they can even convert living troops into undead during army preparation – enabling long-term strategies based on sacrifice and resurrection.
[/p][h2]Expanding the RPG Side of Stormbinders[/h2][p]
Just like in the classic Heroes games, we’ve added a deep RPG layer to our heroes. Each one is more than just an army leader – they have a class, a backstory, a unique skill tree, and their own strengths and weaknesses. Who you choose matters. How you build them changes the whole game.[/p][p]Each faction comes with special hero classes available only to them:[/p][list][*][p]Helion: Firecallers and Demon Champions[/p][/*][*][p]Astrion: Stormmasters and Arcanists[/p][/*][*][p]Empyrium: Paladins and Mages[/p][/*][*][p]Immortus: Necromancers and Death Knights[/p][/*][/list][p]These aren’t just different titles – each class has a unique set of stats, spells, and development paths. They define how you fight and what tools you bring to the field.
[/p][h2]Looking Ahead[/h2][p]
This entry bridges the philosophical and the mechanical—from the beliefs that shape each faction to the powers they wield and the heroes they lead. In our next dev diary, we’ll continue this thread by diving into how hero classes and ability trees are designed, and what makes each one feel distinct in combat and campaign play.[/p][p]See you in the next Dev Diary![/p][p][/p][p][b]Wishlist Stormbinders[/b]
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #3: Factions Overview
notes.content:
[p]In this third dev diary, we’re diving into the heart of Stormbinders’ core experience: its four factions. You’ll get an overview of the four major factions, their playstyles, unique faction abilities, and the creative thinking behind their unit designs.
[/p][h2]Empyrium [/h2][previewyoutube="rmK4ca1M5-Q;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Once a strong and united kingdom, Empyrium is now divided and troubled by betrayal. It is a human faction trying to stay in control in a world full of magic and chaos. Their greatest strength is flexibility – they can adapt to any situation.
[/p][h3]Playstyle[i]
[/i][/h3][p]Empyrium is a human faction that mixes tradition with new ideas. They have a balanced army and a strong economy, which helps them control the pace of the game. They are good at both defending and attacking. This faction is great for players who enjoy a well-rounded and flexible playstyle.
[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfybV95tRFnyejpENcsIAmCaVIFjwd9it4gohxY0BTJ0tSjETZprL1Spm9rKGB-hRqaigOAqOs8-w8ArrsfQG-8CTNdu0TMtrpQdfuon7uK2t9T6DYCwDBbozNPeDOAUps-4Qts2ODTeU03IatzlZk?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc-IGLl2yq3blEmWPWMOKfdN2W6gxegnzJudr3E4BBg6Ak73HY_IPCwSvnw-91u-I67p1eXy9AB-XcsUEcgTqvvMFW0mC0RVdC6uo1XMxdpUBG8OW6stOOml1k7H1tkl8IU4u567l0MHRYPG_3ElyY?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf1-5OQI1Abk_fqCI9z7ADadFp-DjCS2Cno2nHywJhLO1-nKC1QfpLAv9EcTjA18xDlzm8w5KBv5ShDxTDADtuH1Kke1vUaF7n8ftVW8mx8FeSVbPq7gb2V9rTMVLJTO7xrmp24vA9VbM_fBl0IkA?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][/p][h3]Faction Ability[/h3][p]
Empyrium has a unique power that lets them bring back fallen living units. Using the power of the Sun and advanced technology, they can return soldiers to the battlefield at key moments. When used wisely, this ability can completely change the outcome of a battle.[/p][p][/p][h2]Astrion [/h2][previewyoutube="dUHPv_tzwyU;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Astrion is a faction built on harmony, knowledge, and the protection of the world’s magical balance. Long ago, their people became the first to understand the power of the Magic Weave—the hidden threads that keep reality stable. They became guardians of this force, creating powerful cities, magical towers, and schools to study and protect it.[/p][p][/p][h3]Playstyle[/h3][p]
Astrion armies are small but powerful. They don’t rely on large numbers—instead, they use strong, well-trained units with magic support. They are best for players who like to protect their troops, plan carefully, and win through control and smart decisions.[/p][p]Every unit lost matters. Every spell counts. Astrion rewards players who are careful, defensive, and clever with their moves.[/p][p][i][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdzpbLt9VFoaVkmBLyy_pNJMKXeqJ74kAwXJW9j1gt4gqa6-4fG-S7r-r2QSXXQoCub-q81HTQtYA_GB37zHFVUI0YkTSP4UdiaspHALtm-5pKUDUbJPfED57GETMkgw1znbn6YyPXzxBJx8xS1WQ?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][/i][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd8M4SQOzK3qPU0XqHLmmewB_fkp-tofQFPBR7Z7ghHl7zr_Fz42nLqKZT8XznSYMqjWaksgIkcBphzemlPGTR7IDbpJfF7dgxEy27jFLZqmmLWhjWwv0wIrvD2cEG4FBIGUvwz32NA64B-OLuH650?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeZCR6uqd9Tf9rctCQkflbKJaBaVUmrJQTJfBdvxKtCMiia7WwvA5d9BOGVl2L_OGpbOYlx51Z6YyM_mAuuWu_oj340yuLONTXWeg62xBZle50uBHbrgcrKUaO3QY5F9Ipy3zSSIwyFtgt_nxP0Xw?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][/p][h3]Faction Ability[/h3][p]
Astrion’s unique power is their deep connection to the world’s storms and the Magic Weave. During magical storms, they can channel energy directly from the Weave, making their spells much stronger.[/p][p]This lets them cast stronger shields, control the battlefield with magical effects, and turn the tide of battle when the storm is at its peak. They are the masters of magical timing and control.
[/p][h2]Helion[/h2][previewyoutube="UG8HUgTq2Pc;full"][/previewyoutube][p]The burning armies of Helion, led by Lord Malgrim, show no mercy. This is a faction that doesn’t want to fix the world—they want to burn it down and rebuild it in their own image. Chaos is not a problem for them. It’s a weapon.[/p][p]Helion comes from a realm of fire and destruction. When the magic storms began, they saw their chance. They crossed into the real world, bringing with them fire, demons, and dark magic.[/p][p][/p][h3]Playstyle[/h3][p]
Helion is made for players who enjoy fast, aggressive gameplay. Their strategy is simple: attack, summon, and destroy. They use fire magic to burn their enemies and open portals to summon demons from the Inferno.[/p][p]They reward players who never stop pushing. If you like rushing your enemies, making bold choices, and creating constant pressure—Helion is your faction. They love chaos and know how to turn it into strength.[/p][h3][i][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf75YT5YBlGLv7LoSi9KK1TMDeBYv_xsnhQJ2uk1mjwfJcjOAs8jNZcmf0klK13683ibcaCNuxDiwIkKihs42fdXJ64AeN-jZbQdSbVzLxObnsZbjt-zc008Xx-TBI-FylUG-rS1S3spwKjtmkRPlE?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdTmRKgMx6mvz50m_2PfbcYZlV0CiWYIdA5ET7wvlLIiGmfNhbL2VM9ehGKiuTMuCmbaxu-vae7y4t2i8EBK0nlloFik_Ib0jIJ3te8BboEQkGLQl-RNwg456fQERdkqny7tKf2c9brYuYDDsQBsGk?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc42nzqneFlWP3O5-Usxx4Pds3AvulwrJC8qN9UhFQep29iKWvCuEvNteHmDgyzackFrbV16wj8hD3iUUl7xeCcFcWsE0IjzIQTfVO1m7pS1Kp1vU1S9w73joRTiWqElhBD41sW_1-B1a5H1BbGoAQ?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img]
[/i]Faction Ability[/h3][p]
Helion has a unique power: they can absorb the souls of defeated enemies. These souls are turned into [b]demonic energy[/b], which can be used to power up spells or summon more units from the depths of Hell.[/p][p]The longer a battle goes on, the stronger Helion becomes. Every kill fuels their army. In the end, nothing is left but flames, ash, and demons.
[/p][h2]Immortus[/h2][previewyoutube="n2gfQ-Er5w8;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Immortus is a faction of the undead. They believe that death is not the end—it’s just a new form of life. Their leader, the necromancer Skuld, commands an army of bones and spirits, all working to restore the natural order that has been broken.[/p][p]They do not fear death—they control it.[/p][p][/p][h3]Playstyle[/h3][p]
Immortus wins by numbers. Their units are weak alone, but they are cheap and many. With necromancy, every battle helps them grow stronger. Every fallen unit—friend or enemy—can rise again as a skeleton under your command.[/p][p]This is a great faction for players who enjoy slow, steady control. If you like to wear down enemies over time, build giant armies, and take control of the battlefield, Immortus is for you.[/p][h3][i][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXewY57EyoF83l0T9hqsZv2JeMHqkgCuuCkbvO3eZYAzY_-iGnkKG4izf6wKQu7dwKM8Qc4dm2YC_bfJaOr8fKhXNCFujZ0EpLcXKq3Xr_wbMqnjfgwhwfvVNdgqkOom6-an4eHCg5_HmzZmWZ8Oijw?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf1kmcX1R7U4Pjw2rHonciJQ3ASi4PmBiMMmiNl6mWZy00jVwcg77b3QOh-UBJ7D215gmdm8q3nK-bjPKweGjpJBUFuEEKDUX_v8HrPe7lW9pvFZbj7vCJUKf_rcVve3gRoEAUVp0f86RKQVRULFKo?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdu-PiEeVOND8ogmbuEtNQs2aPth1vgfPInI36ytMEG2uYJTDGrmmz0bEGtCcA0smxTNHcLzRuWNYJ4sl5stkKJUti2_iEcBAG8sno8ZJyYH4uBg0pTrPIrb0ZmnUGUygV21mq_rxIXFDaqtADOZ3Q?key=PKHohLmtTofa9t5HRVutsg"][/img][/i]Faction Ability[/h3][p]
Every unit that dies in battle can come back as a skeleton and join your army. Even better, with their special building [b]Pit of Bones[/b], you can turn living units into undead before the fight even begins. This lets you grow your army in new ways.[/p][p][/p][h2]Units design [/h2][p]
Each faction in [i]Stormbinders[/i] has a full set of units - from more “classic” monsters to wild beasts and humanoid creatures. But we didn’t just assign random monster types to each group. We asked ourselves: [i]Does this unit feel right? Does it match the mood of the faction? Is it cool?[/i][/p][p]That “vibe” was our starting point.[/p][p]From there, we built unique rosters that make each faction feel different. You’ll find creatures in [i]Stormbinders[/i] that rarely - or never - appear in other games. We believe the world of monsters is huge, and we wanted to explore it fully.[/p][p]For example: [b]Astrion[/b] has many desert beasts and magical units. These match their faction’s themes of survival, mystery, and power.[/p][p]Their unique faction ability lets them [b]revive fallen living units[/b], and their buildings focus on [b]battlefield control and strategy[/b]. Whether you play aggressively or defensively, Empyrium always has a tool for the job.[/p][p][/p][h2]Summary [/h2][p]
Stormbinders’ four factions offer players a rich mix of strategic depth, thematic storytelling, and distinct playstyles. Inspired by proven ideas, we’ve added our own twist, blending familiar mechanics with fresh systems. The result is a game where experienced players will feel right at home, while still finding plenty of new dynamics to discover. From magical precision to chaotic firepower, each faction feels unique both narratively and mechanically. [/p][p]This foundation is central to how we’re building the world, and we can’t wait to share more.[/p][p]See you in the next Dev Diary!

[b]Wishlist Stormbinders
[/b][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2134720/Stormbinders/"][/dynamiclink]
[/p]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #2: Beyond the Classics
notes.content:
We know many of you grew up with games like Heroes of Might and Magic, Disciples, or Age of Wonders, just like us. But from the start, we knew we weren’t here to recreate what’s already been done.

We asked ourselves not, “How do we remake a classic?” but rather: “What’s next for turn-based strategy? What else can we add to this genre before it becomes stale?” 

And after many tests and ideas, we landed on something surprisingly simple: There’s never really been a strategy game with a dynamic weather system, one with changing weather, magical storms, and chaotic elements that can either be harnessed or feared.

That’s how Stormbinders was born. 

[h3]Stormbinding Features [/h3]
At the center of the game is our stormbinding system — a system means weather is not just decoration, but becomes part of gameplay. It changes the map, the missions, the experience; and therefore your strategy and your choices. 
[list]
[*] It’s not just about snow falling or dust rising
[*] It’s about how ice forms on rivers in winter and lets you cross them in new ways
[*] It’s about lightning storms that grow and might block movement on the map
[*] It’s about how spells behave differently depending on the season — stronger, weaker, or with unique new effects
[*] It’s about how a smart opponent can build their hero to use the weather — and win with a smaller army if you don’t plan around the storm
[/list]
Stormbinding adds atmosphere, but more importantly, it adds new tactical depth — easy to learn, hard to master. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/8890e2f486aace40baa76407dd75e2e469242972.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/1d7899b659ad7c4e26187afa1bc671c82dff779a.jpg[/img]
[h3]For the Players Who Love Outplaying Their Enemies[/h3]
If you're the kind of player who loves planning and optimization, Stormbinders has a lot for you.
[list]
[*] You can build armies that resist certain types of storms
[*] You can use terrain to your advantage. (Why not try freezing the lake during a water storm and sneak into the enemy castle?)
[*] You can learn and control weather patterns and build your entire strategy around them
[/list]
Behind every decision, there’s a system. Behind every result, there’s a number.
But if you prefer to play by instinct, that’s totally fine too. Stormbinders rewards smart choices but doesn’t punish casual play.
Each biome has its own rules, and every storm behaves differently depending on where it strikes. Of course, we’ve also packed the game with tons of talents, perks, upgrades, and gear sets, many of which cancel each other out and are fully customizable.

So yes, expect those crazy combos where, if done right, you can two-shot a stack of high-tier units.
Why? Because you stacked Buff A, Buff B, Buff C, wore Set D, and became an unstoppable Fire Mage… until Player B stormbinds a weather shift that nullifies all fire magic.

[i]Tough luck.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/3513a18d1d18fca97482445d31991a3289406e56.jpg[/img]
[h3]Customizations[/h3]
New Systems? Yes, but Only If You Want 
Not everyone wants to learn new systems. Some people just want a classic strategy game with a good map and fun combat. 
That’s fine. That’s why you can turn off various elements, choose “always winter” maps, or play in “classic mode” if that’s your style.
Everything is optional and customizable. We believe players should decide how deep they want to go  (Screw the Designers, they don’t know how YOU would like to play).  

[h3]Nostalgia Meets the Unexpected[/h3]
We took systems you already know and love and added something new that makes the game feel much more dynamic, even though it’s still firmly turn-based at its core. 
Yes, it’s still a strategy game. But sometimes, your biggest enemy isn’t another player… it’s the weather you didn’t plan for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/eb7247e2c069202da607dee95b481d964a3ff800.png[/img]

notes.title: Stormbinders - Dev Diary #1: Introduction to the Lore
notes.content:
A few weeks ago, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2134720/view/500570289903501660]we revealed Stormbinders[/url]. Today, we're kicking off a series of dev diaries to dive deeper into its world, starting with a look at the lore and creative vision behind the game.

This first entry includes conceptual art pieces to help set the tone and atmosphere of the game. As the series continues, we’ll dive deeper into gameplay systems, tools, and footage, giving you a closer look at what the team is working hard to bring to life.

Let’s begin!

[h3]The World and the Weave[/h3]
Everything in this world is connected by something called the [b]Magic Weave[/b]. It’s not just magic, it’s life itself. It controls emotions, growth, decay, even the weather. It keeps nature breathing and time flowing.

But something has gone terribly wrong.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/089c7efdafc44844318460b0ecfad003a2bc709c.jpg[/img]
The weave is broken. No one knows why, or who caused it. But the effects are everywhere. Magic lashes out in wild surges. Storms arrive without warning. The dead stir. People dream of fire falling from the sky. Some say the world is ending. Others say it’s just changing.

Across the land, cracks called [b]rifts[/b] have opened: places where raw, unstable magic pours through. Around them, nothing is normal. Weather, time, and life twist into strange shapes. The rifts are dangerous, but they also hold answers. And power.

[h3]The Stormbinders[/h3]
In this age of chaos, a few individuals have begun to hear the storm, and bend it to their will. You are one of them. You are a [b]Stormbinder[/b].

The bond between you and the weave is still alive. While others fear the wild weather, you feel it responding to your thoughts. You can guide it. Shape it. Call it forth in battle. Where armies clash, you summon rain to heal your troops. When enemies rise, you bring down thunder. In the cold silence of a ruined forest, you breathe snow into the wind to slow your foes.

You don’t cast spells like others. You [b]bind the storm[/b] itself.

But this power is not safe. It grows, it pulls at you. And the more you use it, the more the world around you begins to shift in your presence.

[h3]A Fractured World[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/fc7f4dfe1913a2c9b9bd378a06c31facdd64bb00.jpg[/img]
Each land has changed in its own way.

In [b]Astrion[/b], scholars and mystics try to protect what remains of the weave. Their forests, once peaceful, are now filled with unstable magic. Their cities struggle to hold together under the weight of too many questions and not enough time.
They believe in knowledge, harmony, and the idea that magic should serve the world—not rule it.

From the flames of [b]Helion[/b], the demon lord Malgrim sees the broken weave as an opportunity. With fire and fury, he marches to conquer. He doesn’t want to fix the world—he wants to reshape it in his image.
Helion thrives in chaos. To them, destruction is just the first step toward rebirth through dominance.

To the north, in the cold silence of [b]Immortus[/b], the dead whisper and walk. Their leaders believe this is part of a natural cycle. They say life and death are not enemies, just two halves of the same breath. If the weave is to be restored, it must be done their way.
Immortus seeks balance not through peace, but through acceptance of decay, death, and renewal.

And in the proud cities of [b]Empyrium[/b], a kingdom once ruled by light now sits in shadow. Betrayed from within, unsure who to trust, their future lies in the hands of a broken king and a young heir no one expected.
Once symbols of order and divine right, Empyrium now stands at the edge of collapse—its pride clashing with its guilt.

[h3]The Heart of the Conflict[/h3]
All these lands are connected through the weave—and all are suffering as it unravels. Some want to heal it. Some want to use it. Others want to let it die.

And in the middle of it all stands you, the Stormbinder.

Where others fight with swords or spells, you carry the storm. You can mend what is broken. Or you can bring even greater ruin.

The storms are not just tools. They are alive. They remember. And they are watching what you choose to do with them.

[h3]What Awaits You[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/d1d0299a332cf9276244717ddeb2a72b5a210f33.jpg[/img]
Your journey will take you across burning deserts, frozen wastelands, ruined temples, and storm-scarred cities. You will meet heroes and traitors. You will chase secrets buried in ancient ruins and rifts that tear the sky open. The choices you make will ripple through the weave.

This is not just a story about war. It’s a story about what survives after the storm. And who controls what comes next.

You are not a chosen one. You are not the last hope.
You are the storm’s voice.

And the world is listening.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45554526/bab9ed020914f56a21e3e61b46693c1bff887b9a.jpg[/img]
Thank you for following along! Stay tuned for our next dev diary, where we’ll explore our inspirations from heroes: what we learned and how we’re innovating beyond the classics.

notes.title: Heroes of Might and Magic gets successor in new strategy game Stormbinders
notes.content:
At first glance, you'd be forgiven for assuming that Stormbinders was a new Heroes of Might and Magic game. High fantasy? Check. Turn-based action? Check. Hexagonal grids galore? Triple check. But Slitherine's latest isn't just a carbon copy of the Ubisoft classic: it adds a brand new mechanic that not only changes the game entirely, but tests your mettle in unique ways. If you're looking for a new challenge, this one's for you.
